item.title: What's gone up even faster than gas or rent? The cost of caregiving
item.description: A new study from AARP shows caregivers' out-of-pocket costs rose about 60% in the last five years.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Are you an organ donor? Here are some rule changes you may want to know
item.description: Transplant teams can talk to families about organ donation before they've decided whether to continue life-sustaining medical care for loved ones. Until now, that has been forbidden.
item.content:encoded: Transplant teams can talk to families about organ donation before they've decided whether to continue life-sustaining medical care for loved ones. Until now, that has been forbidden.

item.title: Some people with meat allergies from alpha-gal syndrome turn to exotic alternatives
item.description: People with alpha-gal syndrome can have allergic reactions to meat from mammals. Many of those affected change their diets to eat other proteins.

item.title: The Ebola outbreak is breaking records -- and just marked a grim milestone
item.description: The current outbreak, first identified in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has now counted 10,000 patients and has spread with great speed. How can it be stopped?

item.title: Special ed diaries: Teachers tell NPR about their most joyous, most difficult moments
item.description: What makes special education teaching jobs so hard to fill? NPR set out to find some answers by talking to more than a dozen teachers who do this work every day.
item.content:encoded:
Bottom row (from left): Paul Stone of Mt. Diablo Unified School District in California, Diana Swanson of Vail School District in Arizona, Kathleen Tejeda of Alvord Unified School District in California and Emily Ellis of Lexington School District Two in South Carolina.'/>

item.title: Merck's melanoma vaccine trial shows reduced recurrence or death from skin cancer
item.description: Merck presented its mRNA melanoma vaccine trial data at a European cancer conference this weekend. Results are promising: The vaccine reduces recurrence and death alongside an immunotherapy drug.

item.title: U.S. measles cases more than double what they were last year as outbreak spreads
item.description: Pennsylvania is the worst hit state, with at least 1,338 cases of measles confirmed in 44 counties so far this year, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health.
